```{r}
set.seed(1)
```

R has a very wide range of functions and packages for visualising data. The chapters in this part start with [plotting in R](ggplot.qmd), from base graphics to ggplot2, and [combining several plots into one figure](multi-panel-figures.qmd). They then cover spatial data and maps, and [heatmaps](heatmaps.qmd). Plots for multivariate data are covered alongside the analyses they come from.

## Visualising multivariate data

```{r}
#| label: multivariate-vis-1
#| fig-alt: "Two example multivariate plots side by side: an MDS ordination with points coloured by habitat forming distinct groups, and a cluster dendrogram of samples with labels coloured by location"
#| echo: false
#| fig-width: 8
#| fig-height: 4
#| warning: false
#| message: false

Herbivores <- read.csv(file = "data/Herbivore_specialisation.csv", header = TRUE)

par(mfrow = c(1, 2))

# MDS ordination

Habitat <- Herbivores$Habitat
Herb_community <- Herbivores[, 4:10]
library(vegan)
Herb_community.mds <- metaMDS(comm = Herb_community, distance = "bray", trace = FALSE)
plot(Herb_community.mds$points, col = as.factor(Habitat), pch = 16, xlab = "", ylab = "", xaxt = "n", yaxt = "n")

# Cluster diagram

library(dendextend)
Harbour_metals <- read.csv(file = "data/Harbour_metals.csv", header = TRUE)
Harbour_metals2 <- Harbour_metals[, 4:8]
rownames(Harbour_metals2) <- Harbour_metals$Rep
H_metals.sim <- dist(Harbour_metals2, method = "euclidean")
H_metals.cluster <- hclust(H_metals.sim, method = "single")
dend <- as.dendrogram(H_metals.cluster)
sample_colours <- as.numeric(factor(Harbour_metals$Location))
sample_colours <- sample_colours[order.dendrogram(dend)]
labels_colors(dend) <- sample_colours
plot(dend, ylab = "")
```

Data with many variables per sample, such as the abundances of many species at each site, are usually visualised by reducing them to a few dimensions or by grouping similar samples. These plots are covered in the [Multivariate and Other Methods](../statistical-methods/multivariate-methods.qmd) part, with the analyses that produce them:

* [multidimensional scaling](../statistical-methods/mds.qmd)
* [principal components analysis](../statistical-methods/pca.qmd)
* [cluster analysis](../statistical-methods/cluster-analysis.qmd)
